title: Gujeoram Hermitage: A Quiet Bamboo-Forest Hideaway Near Hongseong
html:
Most first-time visitors to Korea stick to Seoul and Busan — and that's a great start. But if you want to see a quieter, more local side of the country, small countryside temples like Gujeoram Hermitage (구절암, pronounced roughly "goo-jeo-ram") are where you'll find it. It's a tiny Buddhist hermitage tucked into a bamboo forest in Hongseong, a rural county about two hours southwest of Seoul. There's no entrance fee, no crowds, and almost no English information online — so this guide covers everything you need to actually get there and know what to expect.

What Is Gujeoram Hermitage?

A "hermitage" (암, -am, in Korean temple names) is a small, simple place of worship — think of it as a miniature temple, often with just one or two halls, usually run by a handful of monks or caretakers rather than a large community. Gujeoram sits partway up a small mountain in Guhang-myeon, a rural district of Hongseong County, surrounded by a bamboo forest. There's no entrance fee, and it's open year-round. Don't expect a grand, ornate complex like the famous temples you'll see in guidebooks — the appeal here is the opposite: a peaceful, unpolished spot where you can hear the wind move through the bamboo and have the place almost entirely to yourself.

Photo: Korea Tourism Organization (TourAPI data)

Getting To Hongseong From Seoul

Hongseong isn't on the KTX high-speed line, so you have two main ways to get there from Seoul. The easiest is the intercity bus from Seoul's Central City Bus Terminal (next to Express Bus Terminal Station) straight to Hongseong Bus Terminal — it takes about 2 hours. The other option is by train: take the KTX or SRT to Cheonan-Asan Station, then transfer to a local ITX-Mugunghwa train on to Hongseong Station. Either way, book your onward bus or train on an app like Korail (for trains) or search "Seoul to Hongseong" on Kakao Map or Naver Map — both show live timetables in English-friendly map view, even if the booking page itself is in Korean.

Photo: Korea Tourism Organization (TourAPI data)

The Last Stretch: Finding Gujeoram Itself

This is the part most travel guides skip, and it matters: the road up to Gujeoram Hermitage is narrow, winding, and has no signs pointing the way. There's no public bus that goes all the way up — from Hongseong Bus Terminal or Hongseong Station, your best option is a taxi (ask the driver for "구절암," showing them the address helps) or a rental car with navigation. Type the address — 163 Geobuk-ro 218beon-gil, Guhang-myeon, Hongseong-gun — directly into Kakao Map or Naver Map (Google Maps is unreliable for small rural spots in Korea), and follow it closely since there's nobody around to ask for directions once you're on the mountain road. If you get stuck, the hermitage's contact number is +82-41-642-0702.

Photo: Korea Tourism Organization (TourAPI data)

What To Expect & Simple Etiquette Tips

Gujeoram is a working place of worship, not a museum, so a little quiet respect goes a long way. Keep your voice down, dress modestly (covered shoulders and knees are a safe rule at any Korean temple or hermitage), and take your shoes off before stepping into any indoor hall. You're welcome to walk around the grounds and bamboo forest freely — there's no set "tour route" here. A local tip: Korean visitors to small hermitages like this one often leave a small cash donation in the box near the main hall, even without being asked — it's not required of visitors, but it's a nice gesture if you'd like to do as locals do.

Photo: Korea Tourism Organization (TourAPI data)

Make It A Day Trip: Nearby Hongseong Highlights

Since Gujeoram itself is a short, quiet visit, pair it with other spots back in central Hongseong (Hongseong-eup) to make a full day of it. Hongju Eupseong Fortress is a restored Joseon-era (Korea's last royal dynasty, 1392–1897) town wall right in town — it's free, open 24 hours, and has a pleasant walking path between its gates. Right next to it, the Hongju Fortress History Museum covers the area's history in an easy, visual way — walk-in visits only, no reservation needed. Both are an easy taxi ride or short walk from Hongseong Bus Terminal, making them a comfortable way to fill out your day before heading back.

Photo: Korea Tourism Organization (TourAPI data)

Seoul to Hongseong: Comparing Your Options

KTX/SRT + Local Train~2 hoursVaries by transferTrain lovers; needs one transfer
